extracted.intended_audience: readers and writers of regional/Irish creative prose (those interested in depicting peasant life and landscape)
extracted.subtask_description: Producing short, impressionistic prose sketches of rural Irish life that foreground local people, customs, language, music, and landscape. Emphasis on sensory detail, vernacular speech, folklore, and episodic scenes rather than extended plot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capture impressions and moments
rubrics_metrics.description: Impressions, with something of the roughness of peasant speech in them and something of the beauty, phases of a moment breathless and fluttering, the mystery of the sea, the thresh of rain, the sun on a bird’s wing, a wayfarer passing—those are the things I sought to capture in this book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor short, evocative vignettes that freeze a moment or mood. Aim for breathless, fluttering phases rather than long abstract exposition; use concrete incident and sensory detail to evoke atmosphere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the roughness and beauty of peasant speech
rubrics_metrics.description: There is something of the roughness of peasant speech in them and something of the beauty ... caught by me here, as in a snare of leaves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include authentic vernacular and local turns of phrase (including Irish where appropriate). Let dialogue and reported speech carry character and local color; preserve roughness rather than smoothing it into standard diction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value sensory/natural detail over abstract wisdom
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless you have seen the sun you cannot know anything. Sunlight is better than wisdom, and the red of the fairy-thimble more than painted fans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize concrete sensory images—light, smell (peat), sound (fiddles, birds), color—over abstract commentary. Use nature to ground meaning and feeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include local customs, work, and material detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptions of turf-cutting, winter-stales, carrying by creel or ass-cart, funeral processions, Mass attendance, turf-stacks, creels, ass-carts, and other everyday practices populate the narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Render everyday labors, rituals, and material artifacts specifically and accurately to create authenticity; show processes (how turf is cut and stacked, how funerals proceed) rather than merely naming them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weave folklore and the unseen naturally into scenes
rubrics_metrics.description: Where there is contact with the unseen in this book, with the mysteries which we feel rather than understand, it is because of some strange thought dropped in strange words from a peasant’s mouth ... Púca-piles, lusmór and beliefs (a shooting star as 'a soul going up out of purgatory').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate local superstitions, folk-belief and supernatural hints as part of lived experience—present them through characters' remarks and small incidents rather than heavy exposition or skepticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat music and oral tradition as structural and atmospheric material
rubrics_metrics.description: Ballad-singers, street-songs, reels, fiddlers, chants and the musical life (tunes like 'The Fanaid Grove', 'Maggie Pickens') recur throughout scenes and shape mood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use songs, tunes, and the cadences of speech to set rhythm and tone in the prose. Reproduce verses, refrains, or musical description to evoke communal life and atmosphere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compose episodic, scene-driven sketches
rubrics_metrics.description: The text consists of many distinct scenes—ballad-singer in the Diamond, turf-cutting at Lochros, a country funeral, walks between villages—each offering a self-contained image or anecdote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure writing as a series of self-contained episodes or sketches that together build a sense of place; each vignette should have a clear sensory focus or human detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observe people with wit, empathy and specific detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Portraits combine humour and tenderness—the benchful of police laughing, women complaining about the singer, a clock crawling along the road, the funeral procession that is colourful yet sorrowful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for humane, often comic but never merely dismissive depiction: notice small gestures, local speech, and incongruities that reveal character; balance colour and sympathy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use landscape and nature as moral/spiritual backdrop
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature is the 'Time-vesture of God.' If we but touch it, we are made holier. The scent of peat, sunlight, water-falls and cliffs frequently frame human action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow the landscape to reflect and amplify emotional or spiritual tones; present natural features as morally and spiritually significant rather than mere scenery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make walking and travel a method of discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: To lie on one’s loin in the sun is all very well, but walking is better. It is over the hill the wonders are.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the narrator's movement—walks, climbs, and journeys—as a device for encountering scenes, people, and observations; discovery through travel structures the narrative perspective.
